branches.en: THE SHELF: a made item, and then one countable item inside a range.
branches.cn: 货架：一件制成品，再细化为系列中可数的一个单品。

branches.en: WORK AND MEDIA: knowledge, reports and films are brought out like goods.
branches.cn: 劳动与媒体：知识、报告与影片也像货物一样被带出来。

branches.en: ARITHMETIC: multiplication brings one number out of two.
branches.cn: 算术：乘法从两个数里带出一个数。

branches.en: WHAT GROWS OR SHAPES: crops grown from land, and people shaped by their time.
branches.cn: 长成或被塑造之物：田里长出的作物，与被时代塑造的人。

intro.en: Product is a Latin participle turned noun, and its prefix and verb stem still build a large English family.
intro.cn: product 是拉丁分词转成的名词，其前缀与动词词干仍在构建一个庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin producere and productum supply the stem, and ducere supplies a whole series of English verbs through its participle ductum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 producere 与 productum 提供词干，ducere 则通过其分词 ductum 提供了一整串英语动词。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of bringing something out.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「把某物带出来」的意思。

items.structure: ducere, duxi, ductum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the idea of leading.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「引导」的意思。

items.example: The Latin verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The participle became a noun in its own right.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词本身变成了名词。

items.example: Water is the product of the reaction.

items.structure: pro- plus ducere, as a verb
items.example: The factory produces parts for bicycles.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产自行车零件。

items.example: Production rose after the line was rebuilt.
items.exampleCN: 生产线改建后产量上升。

items.example: The meeting was short and productive.
items.exampleCN: 这次会议简短而有成效。

items.example: Heat is a by-product of the reaction.
items.exampleCN: 热是这个反应的副产品。

items.example: The producer financed the whole shoot.
items.exampleCN: 制片人资助了整次拍摄。

definition_zh: 生产；产量；制作；（作品的）上演；生成
definition_en: the process of making goods, or the amount made
core_image: 一条流水线把原料一路推成成品，末端的成品箱不断堆高
scene: 工厂把旧线改成两班倒之后，一个月的成品数量翻了一倍。After the second shift was added, monthly production doubled.
sceneCN: 工厂把旧线改成两班倒，一个月的成品数量翻了一倍；句中的 production 指「把原料制成成品的过程及其产出」（第 1 个义项：制造商品的活动）。图中可辨识物件：流水线、成品箱、排班表、计数器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 生产；产量；制作；上演；生成

senses.title: The making of goods
senses.definition: the activity of making goods from materials, especially in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 用材料制造商品的活动，尤指大量制造
senses.example: After the second shift was added, monthly production doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 加上第二班之后，月产量翻了一倍。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to lead forward, so the word begins as bringing something out into being.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前引出」，因此这个词起于「把东西带出来、造出来」。

senses.title: The amount produced
senses.definition: the total quantity of something made in a given period
senses.definitionCN: 某段时期内造出的总量
senses.example: Rice production reached a ten-year high.
senses.exampleCN: 稻米产量达到十年来的最高点。
senses.why: The noun of the process slides into naming its result, so production can be a number.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词滑向指结果，因此 production 可以是一个数字。

senses.title: Economic output of goods and services
senses.titleCN: 经济意义上的商品与服务产出
senses.definition: the creation of goods and services measured as a whole economy's activity
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体经济活动衡量的商品与服务创造
senses.example: The region's production grew faster than its population.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的产出增长快于人口增长。
senses.why: Economics treats the whole making activity as one quantity, which is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把全部制造活动当作一个量，这就是此义。

senses.title: Staging a play or film
senses.titleCN: 戏剧或影视的排演制作
senses.definition: the work of preparing and presenting a play, film or programme
senses.definitionCN: 筹备并呈现戏剧、电影或节目的工作
senses.example: Production on the film took fourteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的制作花了十四个月。
senses.why: A play is brought out before an audience, which is the same leading-forward image in culture.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧被带到观众面前，与文化领域的「引出」意象相同。

senses.title: Bringing forth knowledge or results
senses.definition: the act of generating ideas, evidence or results rather than goods
senses.definitionCN: 产生想法、证据或成果而非货物的行为
senses.example: The lab's production of reliable data made the review possible.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室产出可靠数据，才使这次评审成为可能。
senses.why: Anything brought into existence can be produced, so the word extends from factories to research.
senses.whyCN: 任何被带进存在的东西都可被「生产」，因此这个词从工厂延伸到研究。

senses.title: A bodily substance generated
senses.definition: the generation of a substance by a living body, such as a hormone
senses.definitionCN: 活体生成某种物质，如激素
senses.example: Stress increases the production of cortisol.
senses.exampleCN: 压力会增加皮质醇的生成。
senses.why: Biology keeps the core meaning of bringing something forth, with no factory involved.
senses.whyCN: 生物学保留「带出某物」的核心义，却不涉及工厂。

senses.title: The stage of being made
senses.definition: the stage at which something is being manufactured or filmed
senses.definitionCN: 某物正在被制造或拍摄的阶段
senses.example: The new model is in production but not yet on sale.
senses.exampleCN: 新车型已在生产，但尚未开售。
senses.why: The phrase in production names a phase of the process, which is why it takes a fixed preposition.
senses.whyCN: in production 指过程的一个阶段，因此配固定介词。

senses.title: A particular staged work
senses.definition: a single play, film or show as staged by a company
senses.definitionCN: 某团体排演的一部戏、电影或节目
senses.example: The festival opened with a new production of the opera.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术节以这部歌剧的新制作开幕。
senses.why: The process noun finally stands for one finished work, a countable product of the stage.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词最终指一部成品，成为舞台上可数的产物。

intro.en: Production comes from Latin productio, 'a bringing forth', from producere 'to lead forward', built on pro- 'forward' and ducere 'to lead'. English took it through French in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: production 来自拉丁 productio「带出、引出」，源自动词 producere「向前引出」，由 pro-「向前」与 ducere「引导」构成，十五世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. It gives duct, conduct, introduce, reduce and educate.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」，衍生 duct、conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere produced producere, 'to lead or bring forward, to bring out'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere 构成 producere，意为「向前引出、带出」。

items.en: Productio named a bringing forth or a stretching out; the sense of making goods grew later.
items.cn: productio 指「带出、拉长」；制造货物的意思出现较晚。

items.en: English adopted production through French, at first for bringing something into existence rather than for factories.
items.cn: 英语经法语吸收 production，最初指使某物产生，而非工厂制造。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century industry fixed the modern sense: the making of goods in quantity, measured as output.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪的工业固定了现代义：大量制造货物，并以产出计量。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether the noun came directly from Latin or through French is not settled, and the earliest date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个名词是直接来自拉丁语还是经法语传入，尚无定论；最早年代也是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same lead-forward root that are easily confused; group two holds near words for making and output.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「向前引出」词根、易混的词；第二组是表示制造与产出的近义词。

entries.definition: Same root: the thing that results, while production is the activity or the total amount.
entries.definitionCN: 同根：指产生的那件东西，而 production 指活动或总量。

entries.definition: The verb of making, and as a noun farm goods; it is the action behind production.
entries.definitionCN: 表示制造的动词，作名词时指农产品；是 production 背后的动作。

entries.definition: The one who makes, or the one who organizes a film; it names an agent, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 制造者或组织影片的人；指施动者而非过程。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus production: the making of a copy, or the biological bearing of young.
entries.definitionCN: re-「再」加 production：复制，或生物的繁殖。

entries.definition: What comes out of a process, especially as a measured quantity; it matches sense two closely.
entries.definitionCN: 一个过程的产物，尤指可计量的数量；与第 2 义接近。

entries.definition: Making goods on an industrial scale; it stresses factories and hands, where production is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 工业规模地制造货物；强调工厂与手工，而 production 范围更广。

entries.definition: The producing of something, especially energy or offspring; it is closer to the older sense than to factory output.
entries.definitionCN: 产生某物，尤指能源或后代；比工厂产出更接近较早的词义。

entries.definition: Bringing something into existence, often artistic or original; production may only repeat an existing design.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物产生，常指艺术或原创；production 可能只是重复既有设计。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the lead-forward root, the fixed phrases and the industrial sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「向前引出」词根、固定搭配与工业义。

normal.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'lead': production leads material forward into a product.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere「引导」：生产把材料一路引成产品。

normal.en: The family runs produce, producer, product, productive, productivity and reproduction.
normal.cn: 同族词有 produce、producer、product、productive、productivity 与 reproduction。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: production line, mass production, production costs, in production.
normal.cn: 固定说法：生产线、批量生产、生产成本、在生产中。

normal.en: The same root appears in conduct, introduce, reduce and educate.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate 中。

normal.en: Economics pairs it with consumption: what is made and what is used up.
normal.cn: 经济学把它与消费配对：造出来的与用掉的。

abstract.en: Picture raw bales entering one end of a line and boxes leaving the other.
abstract.cn: 想象原料包从流水线一端进去，成品箱从另一端出来。

abstract.en: Picture a counter that clicks once per finished item all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只计数器，每出一件成品就跳一下，整天不停。

abstract.en: Picture a stage where a script slowly becomes a lit set.
abstract.cn: 想象一方舞台，剧本慢慢变成亮起的布景。

examples.en: The factory raised production without adding a single worker.
examples.cn: 工厂没有增加一名工人就提高了产量。

examples.en: Steel production fell during the third quarter.
examples.cn: 第三季度钢铁产量下降。

examples.en: The new production of the play moved the action to a modern city.
examples.cn: 这部戏的新制作把故事搬到了现代城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ duct（引导）+ ion」——把原料一路引出来，就是生产

root: 拉丁 productio「带出、引出」，来自 producere = pro-（向前）+ ducere「引导」；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bringing-forth: making goods, the amount made, the whole economy's output, a staged work, new knowledge, a bodily substance, the stage of being made and finally one finished production.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「带出」这个动作：制造货物、产量、整体经济产出、舞台制作、新知识、体内物质、正在制造的阶段，最后是一部成品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that carries raw material forward until it emerges as a finished box.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把原料一路送到出口、变成成品箱的线。

branches.en: ACT AND SCALE: one factory's making and a whole economy's making are the same act at different sizes.
branches.cn: 动作与规模：一家工厂的制造与整个经济的制造，是同一动作的不同尺度。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND PHASE: the figure produced and the stage of being produced are two views of one process.
branches.cn: 数量与阶段：造出的数字与正在造的阶段，是同一过程的两种视角。

branches.en: STAGE: preparing a show and one finished staging are the process and its countable result.
branches.cn: 舞台：排演与一部成品，是过程与可数的结果。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: data and ideas are brought forth exactly as goods are.
branches.cn: 知识：数据和想法被带出来，与货物一样。

branches.en: BODY: a gland making a hormone is production with no factory at all.
branches.cn: 身体：腺体生成激素，是完全没有工厂的生产。

intro.en: Production is a Latin noun of leading forward, built from a prefix, a lead-root and an action ending.
intro.cn: production 是由「向前引出」构成的拉丁名词，包含前缀、引导词根与动作词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives conduct, introduce, reduce and educate; pro- adds the forward direction that production keeps.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate；pro- 增添 production 保留的向前方向。

items.example: The prefix sends the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作送向外。

items.example: The root carries the pulling forward.
The verb produced the English produce.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出了英语的 produce。

items.example: The region produces most of the crop.
items.exampleCN: 该地区生产大部分这种作物。

items.example: The product sold out in a week.

items.exampleCN: 那是一个颇有成效的下午。

items.example: Productivity rose with the new tools.
items.exampleCN: 有了新工具，生产率提高了。
博物馆订了一件复制品。

definition_zh: 多产的；富有成效的；有生产能力的
definition_en: producing a good amount of results, goods or growth, or tending to bring something about
core_image: 一棵果树压弯了枝，树下篮子已经装满，旁边还有空篮等着
scene: 这里指「多产的」。 It was the most productive meeting of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 productive 是「富有成效的」（第 1 个义项：能带来大量成果的）；句意：这是全年最有成效的一次会议。图中可辨识物件：压弯的果枝、装满的篮子、旁边空着的篮子。

pos.zh: 多产的；富有成效的；有生产能力的

senses.title: Yielding results
senses.titleCN: 富有成效的：花了时间有回报
senses.definition: producing useful results, especially in relation to the effort spent
senses.definitionCN: 产生有用成果，尤指相对所花精力而言
senses.example: The negotiation was short but productive.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判很短，但富有成效。
senses.why: producere means 'to lead forth'. A productive hour is one that leads something out into the world.
senses.whyCN: producere 意为“引出”。富有成效的一小时，就是把东西引到世上的一小时。

senses.title: Fertile land
senses.titleCN: 多产的土地：种什么长什么
senses.definition: describing soil or land that yields large crops
senses.definitionCN: 描述能产出大量作物的土壤或土地
senses.example: The valley has some of the most productive soil in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷拥有全国最肥沃高产的土地。
senses.why: Agriculture applies the word to the ground itself: the land leads forth crops, which is the original physical image.
senses.whyCN: 农业把这个词用于土地本身：土地引出作物，这正是最初的物理意象。

senses.title: A productive worker
senses.titleCN: 高效的劳动者：干得多、干得好
senses.definition: describing a person who produces a large amount of good work
senses.definitionCN: 描述能产出大量优质工作的人
senses.example: She is productive even when working from home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在家办公时也效率很高。
senses.why: The word moves from fields to people, measuring how much useful work a person brings out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从田地移到人身上，衡量一个人能引出多少有用工作。

senses.title: Medical: productive cough
senses.definition: in medicine, describing a cough that brings up mucus, as opposed to a dry cough
senses.definitionCN: 医学上描述能咳出黏液的咳嗽，与干咳相对
senses.example: A productive cough usually means the airways are clearing.
senses.exampleCN: 有痰的咳嗽通常意味着气道在排出分泌物。
senses.why: Medicine uses the literal sense: the cough produces something. This shows how far the word has travelled from farms.
senses.whyCN: 医学使用字面义：咳嗽产出了东西。由此可见这个词离农田有多远。

senses.title: Productive discussion
senses.titleCN: 有产出的讨论：谈出了东西
senses.definition: describing conversation that generates ideas, decisions or plans
senses.definitionCN: 描述能产生想法、决定或计划的交谈
senses.example: The workshop ended with a productive list of options.
senses.exampleCN: 工作坊结束时得到了一份有产出的选项清单。
senses.why: Meetings are judged by what they lead forth, so the agricultural adjective becomes a judgment on talk.
senses.whyCN: 会议按其“引出什么”来评判，于是农业形容词变成了对谈话的评价。

senses.title: Productive of
senses.definition: in formal usage, followed by of to mean 'tending to bring about a stated result'
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中后接 of，意为“容易带来所述结果”
senses.example: The policy proved productive of unexpected alliances.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策促成了出人意料的联盟。
senses.why: The of construction states the output explicitly, which the bare adjective leaves implicit.
senses.whyCN: of 结构明确说出产物，而单用形容词时产物是隐含的。

senses.title: Productive skills
senses.definition: in language teaching, describing speaking and writing, the skills that produce language rather than receive it
senses.definitionCN: 语言教学中描述说与写，即产出语言而非接收语言的技能
senses.example: The course balances receptive and productive skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程平衡接受性技能与产出性技能。
senses.why: Applied linguistics splits skills by direction. Productive skills send language out; receptive skills take it in.
senses.whyCN: 应用语言学按方向划分技能。产出性技能把语言送出去，接受性技能把语言收进来。

senses.title: Capacity for output
senses.definition: describing the maximum output an economy, factory or system can generate
senses.definitionCN: 描述经济、工厂或系统能产生的最大产出
senses.example: The plant is running below its productive capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂运转低于其生产能力。
senses.why: Capacity language turns the adjective into a ceiling: what could be led forth if everything worked.
senses.whyCN: 产能语言把这个形容词变成上限：一切顺利时能引出多少。

intro.en: Productive comes from Latin productivus 'fit for producing', from producere 'to lead forth' (pro- 'forward' + ducere 'to lead'), plus the English suffix -ive.
intro.cn: productive 来自拉丁 productivus“适于产出的”，源于 producere“向前引出”（pro-“向前”+ ducere“引导”），加英语后缀 -ive。

items.en: ducere 'to lead' is the base of a large family: conduct, reduce, introduce and educate each add a different prefix of direction.
items.cn: ducere“引导”是一大词族的基础：conduct、reduce、introduce、educate 各加不同方向的前缀。

items.en: pro- 'forward' plus ducere gives producere, 'to lead or bring forth'. The physical picture is leading something out.
items.cn: pro-“向前”加 ducere 构成 producere“引出、产生”。物理画面是把东西引出来。

items.en: Later Latin forms productivus on the participle stem product-, meaning 'having the power to produce'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语在分词词干 product- 上构成 productivus，意为“有产出能力的”。

items.en: English adopts productive first for land and then for people, following the agricultural sense.
items.cn: 英语先把这个词用于土地，再用于人，顺着农业义延伸。

items.en: Clinical usage adds productive cough in the 19th century, where the thing produced is mucus.
items.cn: 19 世纪临床用法加入“有痰的咳嗽”，其中被产出之物是黏液。

items.en: In the 20th century productive capacity becomes an economic term, and productive skills a language-teaching term.
items.cn: 20 世纪，“生产能力”成为经济术语，“产出性技能”成为语言教学术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the duct- stem; the near-meaning group all imply good results, differing in what kind of result.
note.cn: 形近组共享 duct- 词干；近义组都暗含好结果，差别在结果种类。

entries.definition: output per unit of input. The noun is the ratio; the adjective describes the thing that yields.
entries.definitionCN: 生产率。名词是比率，形容词描述产出之物。

entries.definition: the item produced, or the result of a process. It is concrete output, not the ability to produce.
entries.definitionCN: 产品；结果。它是具体产出，不是生产能力。

entries.definition: relating to reasoning from general to specific. It shares ducere but uses de- 'down from', and means logic, not output.
entries.definitionCN: 演绎的。共享 ducere，但用 de-“从……向下”，指逻辑推理而非产出。

entries.definition: producing good results, often of discussion or effort. It is close to productive but more metaphorical.
entries.definitionCN: 富有成果的。接近 productive，但更具比喻色彩。

entries.definition: able to produce crops or young. It is the biological version, applied mainly to land and organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 肥沃的；能生育的。是生物学版本，主要用于土地与生物。

entries.definition: achieving results with little waste. It stresses the input side, while productive stresses the output side.
entries.definitionCN: 高效的。强调投入端，而 productive 强调产出端。

entries.definition: producing money. It is specifically financial, while productive may produce ideas, crops or goods.
entries.definitionCN: 赚钱的。专指金钱收益，而 productive 可产出想法、作物或货物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: The stem duct means 'lead', so productive is about what a thing leads forth.
normal.cn: 词干 duct 意为“引导”，所以 productive 关乎“引出什么”。

normal.en: Productive land, productive workers and productive meetings are three fields judged by the same output question.
normal.cn: 高产土地、高效工人、有成效的会议，三个领域都按同一“产出”问题评判。

normal.en: Productive cough is the literal use: the cough brings something up.
normal.cn: 有痰的咳嗽是字面用法：咳嗽把东西带出来。

normal.en: The pair productive skills and receptive skills splits language learning by direction.
normal.cn: 产出性技能与接受性技能按方向划分语言学习。

normal.en: Productive capacity is the ceiling; productivity is the ratio actually achieved.
normal.cn: 生产能力是上限，生产率是实际达到的比率。

abstract.en: Picture a tree so heavy with fruit that a branch touches the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵果实累累、枝条垂到地面的树。

abstract.en: Picture a loom that turns thread into cloth faster than the eye can follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机，把线变成布快得眼睛跟不上。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that ends with a whiteboard full of arrows.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话结束时，白板上画满了箭头。

examples.en: The reform made the tax system more productive.
examples.cn: 这项改革让税收体系更有产出效率。

examples.en: They spent a productive afternoon drafting the plan.
examples.cn: 他们用了一个有成效的下午起草计划。

examples.en: The land here is productive enough to support two harvests.
examples.cn: 这里的土地足够高产，可以支持两季收成。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普若达克提夫”音近 productive：把东西“达”出来、克住懒散、提上产量——能出成果 → productive 多产的

root: 拉丁 pro-“向前”+ ducere“引导”→ producere“引出、产生”；product- 分词词干 + -ive（拉丁 -ivus，表能力）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all judge a thing by what it leads forth, whether crops, work, ideas, mucus or language.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都按“引出什么”来评判，无论引出的是作物、工作、想法、黏液还是语言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch bent down by its own fruit.
core.cn: 核心意象：被自己的果实压弯的枝条。

branches.en: ORIGINAL IMAGE: results in general and crops from soil are the same leading-forth, one abstract and one physical.
branches.cn: 原始意象：一般成果与土地作物是同一种“引出”，一抽象一具体。

branches.en: HUMAN OUTPUT: a worker and a discussion are both judged by what they leave behind.
branches.cn: 人的产出：工人与讨论都按“留下了什么”来评判。

branches.en: MEDICINE: the cough literally produces something, which shows the literal core of the word.
branches.cn: 医学：咳嗽字面上产出了东西，显示了词的字面核心。

branches.en: FORMAL LINK: productive of states the result that the adjective otherwise implies.
branches.cn: 正式连接：productive of 明说结果，而单用形容词时结果是隐含的。

branches.en: DIRECTION AND CEILING: language skills split by output, and capacity names the maximum output.
branches.cn: 方向与上限：语言技能按输出划分，产能命名最大输出。

intro.en: Productive is the Latin stem product- plus -ive. The stem carries 'brought forth', and the suffix marks the capacity to do it.
intro.cn: productive 是拉丁词干 product- 加 -ive。词干携带“被引出”，后缀标记做这件事的能力。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere 'lead' → producere 'bring forth' → productivus. English keeps duct- and adds -ive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere“引导”→ producere“引出”→ productivus。英语保留 duct- 并加 -ive。

items.meaning: the act or amount of making

items.exampleCN: 他们这一天过得很有成效。

items.meaning: to make more than is needed

definition_zh: 生产率；生产力；产出效率
definition_en: the rate at which work produces output, measured as output per unit of labour, land or capital
core_image: 一台机器前站着一名工人，出口处的成品箱一层层堆高，时钟却只走了一小格
scene: 这里指「生产率」。 Productivity rose after the old machines were replaced.
sceneCN: 这里 productivity 是「生产率」（第 1 个义项：单位投入的产出效率）；句意：旧机器更换之后生产率上升了。图中可辨识物件：机器、工人、堆高的成品箱、只走了一小格的时钟。

pos.zh: 生产率；生产力；产出效率

senses.title: Output per input
senses.titleCN: 生产率：一份投入换多少产出
senses.definition: the ratio of output produced to the input used, such as hours worked or land farmed
senses.definitionCN: 产出与所用投入（如工时或耕地）之比
senses.example: Productivity doubled after the assembly line was redesigned.
senses.exampleCN: 装配线重新设计后，生产率翻了一番。
senses.why: producere means 'to lead forth'. Productivity measures how much is led forth from a given effort, which makes it a ratio.
senses.whyCN: producere 意为“向前引出”。生产率衡量一份投入能引出多少产出，所以它是一个比率。

senses.title: Labour productivity
senses.titleCN: 劳动生产率：每人每小时产出
senses.definition: output per hour or per worker, the most common economic measure
senses.definitionCN: 每工时或每人产出，最常见的经济指标
senses.example: Labour productivity in manufacturing grew by three percent.
senses.exampleCN: 制造业劳动生产率增长百分之三。
senses.why: Hours are the denominator economists use most, because labour is the input that can be counted most cleanly.
senses.whyCN: 工时是经济学家最常用的分母，因为劳动是最容易清楚计数的投入。

senses.title: Agricultural productivity
senses.titleCN: 农业生产力：一亩地打多少粮
senses.definition: output per hectare or per farm worker in farming
senses.definitionCN: 农业中每公顷或每个农业劳动者的产出
senses.example: Higher agricultural productivity freed workers for cities.
senses.exampleCN: 农业生产力提高，使劳动者得以流向城市。
senses.why: Land was the original denominator. When yields rise, the same field feeds more people, and that is productivity.
senses.whyCN: 土地是最初的分母。产量提高时，同一块田能养活更多人，这就是生产力。

senses.title: Productivity growth
senses.titleCN: 生产率增长：效率在变好
senses.definition: the rate at which the output-to-input ratio improves over time
senses.definitionCN: 产出与投入之比随时间改善的速度
senses.example: Productivity growth stalled for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 生产率增长停滞了十年。
senses.why: Growth turns a level into a trend. Economists care about the direction because small yearly gains compound.
senses.whyCN: 增长把水平变成趋势。经济学家关心方向，因为每年小幅提升会复利累积。

senses.title: Office productivity
senses.titleCN: 办公效率：工具让你更快
senses.definition: in computing and marketing, the capacity of a person or tool to complete work, as in productivity software
senses.definitionCN: 在计算与营销语境中指人或工具完成工作的能力，如办公效率软件
senses.example: The suite is sold as productivity software.
senses.exampleCN: 这套软件以办公效率软件的名义出售。
senses.why: Software marketing borrowed the economic word and dropped the denominator, so it now means roughly 'gets work done'.
senses.whyCN: 软件营销借用了经济词却去掉了分母，于是现在大致意为“能把活干完”。

senses.title: Total factor productivity
senses.titleCN: 全要素生产率：剩下那部分增长
senses.definition: the part of output growth not explained by more labour or capital, often taken as technical progress
senses.definitionCN: 产出增长中无法由劳动或资本增加解释的部分，常被视为技术进步
senses.example: Total factor productivity explains most long-run growth.
senses.exampleCN: 全要素生产率解释了大部分长期增长。
senses.why: Economics needs a residual for what it cannot measure. The term names that leftover, which is why it is also called the residual.
senses.whyCN: 经济学需要一个“测不出来的剩余”。这个词命名那块剩余，所以它又叫残差。

senses.title: Ecological productivity
senses.titleCN: 生态生产力：生态系统造出多少有机物
senses.definition: in ecology, the rate at which an ecosystem produces biomass, as in primary productivity
senses.definitionCN: 生态学上指生态系统生产生物量的速率，如初级生产力
senses.example: Primary productivity in the lake fell after the bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 水华之后湖水的初级生产力下降。
senses.why: Ecology transfers the ratio from factories to living systems: sunlight and nutrients are the input, biomass is the output.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把比率从工厂搬到生命系统：阳光与养分是投入，生物量是产出。

senses.title: The productivity paradox
senses.titleCN: 生产率悖论：投了电脑却不见增长
senses.definition: the observed mismatch between heavy investment in technology and weak measured productivity growth
senses.definitionCN: 大量技术投入与测得的疲弱生产率增长之间的落差
senses.example: The productivity paradox delayed the promised office revolution.
senses.exampleCN: 生产率悖论推迟了人们许诺的办公革命。
senses.why: Measurement lag explains part of the paradox: gains appear only after work is reorganised around the new tools.
senses.whyCN: 测量滞后解释了部分悖论：只有围绕新工具重组工作后，收益才显现。

intro.en: Productivity comes from Latin producere 'to lead forth, bring out', from pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'to lead'. The abstract noun is productivitas, formed in later Latin.
intro.cn: productivity 来自拉丁 producere“向前引出、产生”，由 pro-“向前”加 ducere“引导”构成，抽象名词 productivitas 为晚期拉丁构成。

items.en: ducere meant 'to lead'. It underlies conduct, reduce, introduce and educate, each with its own prefix direction.
items.cn: ducere 意为“引导”。它支撑 conduct、reduce、introduce、educate，各接不同方向的前缀。

items.en: pro- 'forward' plus ducere gives producere, 'to lead or bring forth'. The image is leading something out into view.
items.cn: pro-“向前”加 ducere 构成 producere“引出、产生”。意象是把东西引出来让人看见。

items.en: The participle productum 'brought forth' gives English product: the thing led out. Production names the leading-out act.
items.cn: 分词 productum“被引出之物”给出英语 product。production 命名“引出”这个动作。

items.en: Later Latin forms productivitas on the adjective productivus, meaning 'having the power to produce'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语以形容词 productivus“有产出能力的”构成 productivitas。

items.en: English adopts productivity in the age of agricultural improvement, first as the quality of being productive.
items.cn: 英语在农业改良时代采用 productivity，最初指“多产的性质”。

items.en: In the 20th century economics fixes the quantitative sense: output divided by input, tracked as a growth series.
items.cn: 20 世纪经济学固定了数量义：产出除以投入，作为增长序列来追踪。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the duc- stem or the -ivity ending; the near-meaning group all concern output, differing in unit and scale.
note.cn: 形近组共享 duc- 词干或 -ivity 结尾；近义组都关乎产出，差别在单位与尺度。

entries.definition: yielding results or output. The adjective describes the worker or land; productivity measures the ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 多产的；有成效的。形容词描述工人或土地，productivity 度量比率。

entries.definition: the total amount produced. It is a quantity, while productivity is that quantity per unit of input.
entries.definitionCN: 产量。它是总量，而 productivity 是每单位投入的产量。

entries.definition: the item produced. It is the noun for what comes out, not for how efficiently it came out.
entries.definitionCN: 产品。它命名产出物，而非产出效率。

entries.definition: the ratio of useful work to the energy or resources spent. It stresses waste avoided, while productivity stresses output per input.
entries.definitionCN: 效率。它强调避免了浪费，而 productivity 强调单位投入的产出。

entries.definition: the amount produced in a period. It is what productivity divides by input.
entries.definitionCN: 产出量。它是 productivity 用来除以投入的那个分子。

entries.definition: the amount harvested from land. It is a physical output, close to productivity when measured per hectare.
entries.definitionCN: 产量。它是土地的实物产出，按公顷衡量时接近 productivity。

entries.definition: the volume passing through a system in a time. It counts flow, not output per unit of effort.
entries.definitionCN: 吞吐量。它统计流量，而非单位投入的产出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'lead' gives 'lead forth', which is the source of produce, product and productivity.
normal.cn: pro-“向前”加 ducere“引导”得“引出”，是 produce、product、productivity 的共同来源。

normal.en: The word is a fraction: output on top, input on the bottom. Every collocation names one of the two halves.
normal.cn: 这个词是一个分数：产出在上，投入在下。每个搭配都在给其中一半命名。

normal.en: Labour productivity puts hours on the bottom; agricultural productivity puts hectares on the bottom.
normal.cn: 劳动生产率把工时放在分母；农业生产力把公顷放在分母。

normal.en: Production is the total; productivity is the total divided by the effort.
normal.cn: production 是总量；productivity 是总量除以投入。

normal.en: The productivity paradox is the puzzle of paying for computers and not seeing the gain in the numbers.
normal.cn: 生产率悖论就是：花了钱买电脑，数字里却看不到收益。

abstract.en: Picture the same basket of apples carried out by fewer hands.
abstract.cn: 想象同样一篮苹果由更少的人手搬出来。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that finishes the shift while the pile of boxes is twice as high.
abstract.cn: 想象一个班次结束时，箱子堆得比原来高一倍。

abstract.en: Picture a field that feeds two families where it once fed one.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田从养活一户人家变成养活两户。

examples.en: Productivity in the port improved when the cranes were automated.
examples.cn: 港口起重机自动化后，生产率提高了。

examples.en: Wage growth has lagged behind productivity growth.
examples.cn: 工资增长落后于生产率增长。

examples.en: Primary productivity is highest in shallow coastal water.
examples.cn: 初级生产力在浅海沿岸水域最高。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普若达克提维梯”音近 productivity：先把东西“达”出来、再“克”住工时、效率就“提”上去 → productivity 生产率

root: 拉丁 pro-“向前”+ ducere“引导”→ producere“引出、产生”；productivus + -itas 构成抽象名词 productivity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure how much comes out for what goes in, and the differences come from which input is counted.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都衡量“进去多少、出来多少”，差别在数的是哪一种投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: more boxes out of the same hours.
core.cn: 核心意象：同样的工时，搬出更多箱子。

branches.en: THE RATIO: the general fraction and the labour version differ only in the denominator.
branches.cn: 比率：一般分数与劳动版本只差分母。

branches.en: LAND: agriculture counts hectares, the oldest input measure.
branches.cn: 土地：农业按公顷计数，是最古老的投入度量。

branches.en: TRENDS AND PUZZLES: growth tracks the ratio over time, and the paradox notes when it fails to move.
branches.cn: 趋势与悖论：增长追踪比率随时间的变化，悖论指出它不动的时候。

branches.en: MARKETING: software drops the denominator and keeps only 'gets work done'.
branches.cn: 营销：软件抽掉了分母，只留下“能把活干完”。

branches.en: RESIDUAL AND BIOMASS: economics and ecology both measure what the obvious inputs cannot explain.
branches.cn: 剩余与生物量：经济学与生态学都度量“明显投入解释不了的部分”。

intro.en: Productivity is productiv- plus -ity. The stem carries 'leading forth', and the suffix turns an adjective of capacity into an abstract measure.
intro.cn: productivity 是 productiv- 加 -ity。词干携带“引出”，后缀把表能力的形容词变成抽象度量。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere 'lead' → producere 'bring forth' → productivus 'producing'. The English family runs produce, product, production, productive, productivity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere“引导”→ producere“引出”→ productivus“有产出能力的”。英语词族为 produce、product、production、productive、productivity。

items.meaning: the act or total of making

items.exampleCN: 这是一次有成效的会议。

items.meaning: in a way that yields results
items.exampleCN: 他们一上午都干得很有成效。

definition_zh: 职业；行业；同业；声明；信仰表白
definition_en: a job that needs special training and a formal qualification, the people who do it, or an open declaration of belief
core_image: 一个人站在众人面前，一手按在胸前，公开说出自己以什么为业、又信什么
scene: 面试官问她靠什么谋生，她说自己受过多年训练，做的是需要执照的活儿。She practises the legal profession in a small coastal town.
sceneCN: 这里表示「需要专门训练的职业」（第 1 个义项：以长期训练和正式资格为基础的谋生行当）；句意为她在一座海滨小城从事法律工作。

derivatives.zh: 由 profession 加 -al 构成，义为「职业的；专业人士」
由 professional 加 -ism 构成，义为「专业水准；职业精神」
与 profession 同出拉丁语 profiteri，义为「公开宣称；声称」

senses.title: A job that requires special training and qualifications
senses.definition: a type of work that needs long training and a formal qualification, such as law or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 需要长期训练与正式资格的工作，如法律或医学
senses.example: She chose teaching as her profession.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择教书作为自己的职业。
senses.why: The Latin source meant to declare openly; a profession is the work one publicly declares as one's own, not a task done quietly and unnamed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「公开宣称」；职业就是一个人当众声明属于自己的那份工作，而不是默默无名地做的杂活。

senses.title: The whole group of people who do such work
senses.definition: all the people who work in one such field, considered as a body with shared standards
senses.definitionCN: 在某一此类领域工作的所有人，被视为拥有共同标准的一个整体
senses.example: The medical profession opposed the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 医学界反对这些新规定。
senses.why: If a profession is what each member declares, the same word can name the company of all who make that declaration.
senses.whyCN: 既然职业是每个成员公开认领的东西，同一个词也就能指所有做出这一认领的人所组成的群体。

senses.title: A solemn declaration of religious faith
senses.definition: a formal and public statement that one holds a particular religious belief
senses.definitionCN: 公开而正式地表明自己持守某一宗教信仰
senses.example: Her profession of faith was made before the whole congregation.
senses.exampleCN: 她在全体会众面前作了信仰表白。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the Latin verb meant to declare aloud, and the first things declared in that way were matters of belief.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：拉丁动词本义就是「大声声明」，而最早被这样声明的正是信仰上的事。

senses.title: An open claim about one's feelings or intentions
senses.definition: a statement in which someone openly claims to feel or intend something
senses.definitionCN: 某人公开声称自己有某种感受或打算的说法
senses.example: His profession of friendship did not convince anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他声称的友谊没能说服任何人。
senses.why: Once the word means a public declaration, it can carry any claim a person makes aloud, including one that others may doubt.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「公开声明」，它就能承载任何被人大声说出的主张，包括旁人未必相信的那种。

intro.en: Profession and professor grow from the same Latin verb, but one names the declared work and the other the person who declares it.
intro.cn: profession 与 professor 出自同一个拉丁动词，但前者指被公开认领的工作，后者指做这种公开宣称的人。

items.en: Fateri meant to confess or acknowledge, to say something about oneself that others could hear.
items.cn: fateri 意为承认、供认，是把自己身上的事说给别人听。

items.en: Pro- made it public: profiteri meant to declare openly, often a belief or a calling.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 使它变为公开：profiteri 意为公开声明，常指声明信仰或志业。

items.en: The noun professio was a public declaration, and in Roman law it could also be the declared occupation on which tax was paid.
items.cn: 名词 professio 指公开声明；在罗马法中也可指申报并据此纳税的职业。

items.en: Old French profession kept both the religious and the occupational senses and passed them to English.
items.cn: 古法语 profession 同时保留宗教与职业两种含义，并把它们传入英语。

items.en: English uses profession mainly for qualified work and its body, while the older sense of open declaration survives in phrases such as a profession of faith.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用 profession 指需要资格的工作及其群体，而「公开声明」的旧义仍保存在 a profession of faith 这类说法里。

note.en: The first group shows the same Latin verb and its family, including the word for the person who declares; the second gathers words for jobs and for formal statements.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁动词及其词族，包括指「宣称者」的词；第二组收表示工作与正式陈述的词。

entries.definition: To state openly that one has a belief or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 公开表明自己持有某种信仰或感受。

entries.definition: A senior university teacher; literally one who declares publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 资深大学教师；字面义为公开宣称的人。

entries.definition: Relating to a profession, or a person who works in one.
entries.definitionCN: 与职业有关的；从事某一职业的人。

entries.definition: To admit something one would rather keep hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 承认本不愿让人知道的事；坦白。

entries.definition: The job by which a person earns money.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人谋生所从事的工作。

entries.definition: The whole course of a person's working life.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人整个职业生涯的历程。

entries.definition: A skilled job, especially one done with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 需要手艺的工作，尤指手工行业。

entries.definition: A formal statement made in public.
entries.definitionCN: 在公开场合做出的正式陈述。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb of public declaration runs through the whole family, which is why the same word can mean a job and a statement of belief.
normalIntro.cn: 一整族词都建立在同一个表示「公开声明」的拉丁动词上，所以同一个词既能指职业，也能指信仰声明。

normal.en: Fateri is to admit; pro- makes it public, so profiteri is to say openly who you are and what you do.
normal.cn: fateri 是承认，pro- 使之公开，所以 profiteri 就是当众说出自己是谁、做什么。

normal.en: A profession is the work you declare as yours; a professor is the person who declares and teaches.
normal.cn: profession 是你公开认领的工作；professor 是做公开声明并讲授的人。

normal.en: The medical profession means the doctors as a group, because the declared work gathers its members into one body.
normal.cn: the medical profession 指医生这个群体，因为被共同认领的工作把成员聚成了一个整体。

normal.en: A profession of faith keeps the old sense of a spoken declaration, not a job.
normal.cn: a profession of faith 保留的是「口头声明」的旧义，与工作无关。

normal.en: Professional adds -al to profession, turning the field into an adjective or into the person who belongs to it.
normal.cn: professional 在 profession 后加 -al，把这个领域变成形容词，或指属于该领域的人。

abstract.en: A job becomes a profession only when it is publicly named, which suggests that recognition is part of the work itself.
abstract.cn: 一份工作只有被公开命名才成为职业，这说明「被承认」本身就是这份工作的一部分。

abstract.en: The same word covers what you do and what you believe, because both are things you stand up and declare.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既覆盖你做什么，也覆盖你信什么，因为两者都是你站出来声明的东西。

abstract.en: A profession is a promise made in public: that is why its members are held to shared standards.
abstract.cn: 职业是一份当众做出的承诺，所以它的成员要受共同标准的约束。

examples.en: She entered the teaching profession at twenty-two.
examples.cn: 她二十二岁进入教师行业。

examples.en: His profession of loyalty sounded sincere.
examples.cn: 他声称的忠诚听起来很真诚。

examples.en: Members of the legal profession attended the hearing.
examples.cn: 法律界人士出席了听证会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若费神」——挑职业要费神，入错行更费神；记住 profession 是职业。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、公开）+ fateri（承认、供认）→ profiteri（公开声明）→ professio（声明、申报的职业），经古法语 profession 进入英语；与 professor 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a public declaration; from it come the declared job, the body of people who share that job, and the statement of belief or feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开声明」；由此分出被公开认领的职业、共享该职业的群体，以及信仰或情感的表白。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing before a crowd, naming aloud the work he does and the belief he holds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在众人面前，大声说出自己所做的工作与所持的信念。

branches.en: a person naming a calling and a loyalty in the same breath
branches.cn: 同一次开口里既说出志业，也说出忠诚

branches.en: doctors closing ranks behind their common standards
branches.cn: 医生们以共同标准站成一体

branches.en: a congregation listening to a spoken creed
branches.cn: 会众聆听一段口头的信条

branches.en: a young woman choosing law after years of study
branches.cn: 年轻女子在多年学习后选择法律

branches.en: a claim of friendship that others quietly doubt
branches.cn: 旁人暗自怀疑的友谊表白

intro.en: A Latin verb of admitting, its public prefix, and the noun and adjective endings built on them hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「承认」的拉丁动词、表示公开的前缀，以及建立其上的名词与形容词词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 职业的；专业的；专职的；专业人员；行家；（体育）职业选手
definition_en: relating to a paid occupation, or showing the skill and standards expected in one
core_image: 一件熨得笔挺的白大褂，胸口别着写有姓名的工牌
scene: 手术室里，主刀医生动作稳而快。Every step was measured and every cut was clean, and the assistant called that level of care professional.
sceneCN: 这里 professional 是「专业的、达到职业水准的」（第 3 个义项：具备职业所需的技能与规范）；句意：每一步都经过斟酌，每一刀都干净利落，助手把这种水准称为专业。图中可辨识物件：手术台、无影灯、器械盘、白大褂、工牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 职业的；专业的；专职的；合乎职业规范的
专业人员；行家；（体育）职业选手

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 不专业的；违反职业规范的

senses.title: Relating to a profession
senses.definition: connected with a profession or its members
senses.definitionCN: 与某个职业或其成员相关
senses.example: professional bodies set entry exams.
senses.exampleCN: 行业机构设置入行考试。
senses.why: Profession comes from Latin professio, 'a public declaration'. A professional was first someone who had publicly declared a calling, which is why the word implies a recognized field.
senses.whyCN: profession 来自拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”。professional 最初指公开宣告某种志业的人，所以这个词隐含一个被承认的领域。

senses.title: Done as a paid occupation
senses.definition: engaged in for payment rather than as a hobby
senses.definitionCN: 为报酬而从事，而非作为爱好
senses.example: She is a professional musician.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一名职业音乐家。
senses.why: The 18c. sharpened the contrast with amateur: a professional is paid, an amateur is not. Money becomes the marker that separates the two.
senses.whyCN: 18 世纪强化了与 amateur 的对比：professional 拿钱，业余者不拿。金钱成了区分两者的标记。

senses.title: Competent and skillful
senses.definition: showing the skill and care expected of a trained person
senses.definitionCN: 表现出受训者应有的技能与用心
senses.example: That was a very professional repair job.
senses.exampleCN: 那次维修做得非常专业。
senses.why: Skill turns the label into a compliment: work is professional when it meets the standard a paying client would expect. The word moves from status to quality.
senses.whyCN: 技能把这个标签变成赞美：当工作达到付费客户期待的标准，它就是专业的。这个词从身份转向品质。

senses.title: A member of a profession
senses.definition: a person who works in a profession, especially a learned one
senses.definitionCN: 从事某一职业的人，尤指需要专门学识者
senses.example: The panel included doctors and other professionals.
senses.exampleCN: 专家组包括医生及其他专业人员。
senses.why: The noun names the person behind the adjective. In modern English it often covers lawyers, doctors, engineers, and accountants — fields with entry rules and codes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名形容词背后的人。现代英语中它常涵盖律师、医生、工程师、会计师——有准入规则与职业准则的领域。

senses.title: An expert in a field
senses.definition: a person with high skill in some activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某项活动中技能很高的人
senses.example: He is a professional when it comes to chess.
senses.exampleCN: 在国际象棋上他是个行家。
senses.why: The word can leave the salaried professions behind and simply mean 'someone who really knows'. This looser use turns expertise itself into the qualification.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以离开领薪的职业，只表示“真正懂行的人”。这种宽松用法把专长本身当成资格。

senses.title: A paid sports player
senses.definition: in sport, a player who is paid to compete
senses.definitionCN: 体育中受薪参赛的选手
senses.example: He turned professional at nineteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十九岁转为职业选手。
senses.why: Sport copied the paid/amateur divide. Turning professional means crossing a line: from playing for love to playing for a living, with different rules and stakes.
senses.whyCN: 体育复制了“受薪／业余”的分界。转为职业，意味着跨过一条线：从为热爱而赛，到为生计而赛，规则与利害都不同。

senses.title: Conforming to professional standards
senses.definition: behaving with the ethics and manners of a profession
senses.definitionCN: 以某职业的伦理与礼节行事
senses.example: Her response was calm and professional.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回应冷静而专业。
senses.why: Conduct is judged, not skill. The word can praise someone who keeps confidences and meets deadlines, even when the task is routine.
senses.whyCN: 这里被评判的是行为，不是技能。即使任务平常，这个词也能赞美守密、守时的人。

senses.title: Of high quality, informally
senses.definition: in informal use, well-made or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：做得好的、像样的
senses.example: They did a professional job on the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把花园弄得相当像样。
senses.why: The compliment has spread beyond occupations: anything done with care can look professional. The word now sells quality as much as status.
senses.whyCN: 这种赞美已超出职业范围：任何用心做成的事都可能显得 professional。这个词现在既卖身份，也卖品质。

senses.title: A euphemism for a sex worker (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a euphemism for a prostitute
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：对妓女的委婉说法
senses.example: The old novel refers to her as a professional.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧小说用 professional 指称她。
senses.why: The 'paid occupation' sense sits close to a taboo, so the euphemism was available. Modern usage avoids it because the main sense has become too respectable to carry the hint.
senses.whyCN: “受薪职业”义接近禁忌，因此这个委婉说法曾可用。现代用法避开它，因为主要义已太体面，承载不了这层暗示。

intro.en: Professional is built on profession, and profession began as a public declaration. Latin profiteri means 'declare openly', from pro- 'forth' plus fateri 'to confess'. A professional is, etymologically, someone who has declared what they do.
intro.cn: professional 建立在 profession 上，而 profession 始于“公开宣告”。拉丁语 profiteri 意为“公开宣称”，由 pro-“向前、出来”加 fateri“承认”构成。从词源看，professional 就是公开宣告自己以何为业的人。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'of or belonging to a profession'.
items.cn: 最早记录为形容词，义为“属于某一职业的”。

items.en: profession (late 14c.) comes from Latin professionem, 'a public declaration', from profiteri 'declare openly'.
items.cn: profession（14 世纪末）来自拉丁语 professionem“公开宣告”，源出 profiteri“公开宣称”。

items.en: profiteri = pro- 'forth, publicly' + fateri 'to confess, admit'. The root fateri also gives confession and fate in related senses.
items.cn: profiteri = pro-“向外、公开”+ fateri“承认、告白”。词根 fateri 还生成 confession 等相关词。

items.en: The sense 'engaged in a profession as a paid calling' is recorded.
items.cn: “以某职业为受薪志业”的义项被记录。

items.en: The noun professional appears for a person who makes a living by a profession.
items.cn: 名词 professional 出现，指以某职业谋生的人。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective from occupations to quality and conduct: professional advice, professional standards, a professional job.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词从职业扩展到品质与行为：professional advice、professional standards、a professional job。

note.en: The first group shares the profession/profiteri stem; the second is about words that also mean skilled or paid.
note.cn: 第一组共享 profession/profiteri 词干，第二组看同样表示“有技能”或“受薪”的词。

entries.definition: a paid occupation requiring training. It is the noun behind professional.
entries.definitionCN: 需要训练的受薪职业。它是 professional 背后的名词。

entries.definition: the standards and conduct of a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 职业标准与职业精神。

entries.definition: a university teacher, literally one who professes a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 大学教授，字面“宣称某学科者”。

entries.definition: a person with special knowledge. It stresses knowledge, not pay or code.
entries.definitionCN: 有专门知识的人。它强调知识，而非报酬或准则。

entries.definition: having trained ability. It says nothing about a profession or payment.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、有能力。它不涉及职业或报酬。

entries.definition: relating to a job. It is neutral and technical, unlike the status-laden professional.
entries.definitionCN: 与工作相关的。它中性、技术性，不像 professional 带身份色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin profiteri 'declare openly', the paid/amateur divide, the professional/professor family, and the modern quality sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 profiteri“公开宣称”、受薪／业余之分、professional/professor 词族，以及现代品质义。

normal.en: Latin profiteri means 'declare openly': a professional has publicly declared what they do.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 profiteri 意为“公开宣称”：professional 已公开宣告自己以何为业。

normal.en: The 18c. made money the test: professionals are paid, amateurs are not.
normal.cn: 18 世纪以金钱为标准：professional 受薪，业余者不受薪。

normal.en: Professor and professional share the root: both publicly profess a field.
normal.cn: professor 与 professional 共享词根：两者都公开宣称某个领域。

normal.en: The word has moved from status to quality: a professional job is simply a job done to a high standard.
normal.cn: 这个词从身份滑向品质：a professional job 就是做得高标准的工作。

normal.en: In sport, turning professional means crossing from playing for love to playing for a living.
normal.cn: 体育中，转为职业意味着从为热爱而赛，跨到为生计而赛。

abstract.en: A profession is a public promise: the declaration is what binds the practitioner to a code.
abstract.cn: 职业是一份公开承诺：宣告把从业者绑定到一套准则上。

abstract.en: Professionalism is a form of trust infrastructure: strangers can rely on you because a field vouches for you.
abstract.cn: 专业精神是一种信任基础设施：陌生人能依赖你，因为一个领域为你背书。

abstract.en: When the word praises quality rather than occupation, it shows how deeply work and identity are fused in modern life.
abstract.cn: 当这个词赞美品质而非职业时，它显示出工作与身份在现代生活中融合得有多深。

examples.en: You should seek professional advice before investing.
examples.cn: 投资前你应当寻求专业建议。

examples.en: She handled the complaint in a professional manner.
examples.cn: 她以专业的方式处理了这起投诉。

examples.en: He became a professional football player at twenty.
examples.cn: 他二十岁时成为职业足球运动员。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若费神”——为了职业扑上去费神打磨 → professional 职业的、专业的

root: 由 profession + -al 构成；profession 来自拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”，源出 profiteri“公开宣称”= pro-“向外”+ fateri“承认”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of professional, all built on a public declaration. The declaration can name an occupation, mark payment, certify skill, impose conduct, or simply advertise quality.
sensesIntro.cn: professional 的九个义项都建立在一次公开宣告上。这次宣告可以命名职业、标记受薪、证明技能、施加行为准则，或仅仅为品质作广告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a public declaration that binds a person to a standard.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次公开宣告，把人绑定到某个标准上。

branches.en: FIELD: a recognized occupation and the people who belong to it.
branches.cn: 领域：被承认的职业及其成员。

branches.en: PAY: the paid/amateur line, in work and in sport.
branches.cn: 报酬：工作与体育中的受薪／业余分界。

branches.en: SKILL: training shows as competence, and competence can stand alone as expertise.
branches.cn: 技能：训练表现为胜任，胜任又可单独成为专长。

branches.en: ETHICS: conduct is judged by the standards of the field.
branches.cn: 伦理：行为按该领域的标准被评判。

branches.en: EXTENSIONS: informal praise of quality, and an archaic euphemism that the main sense has outgrown.
branches.cn: 延伸：对品质的非正式赞美，以及主要义已使其不再适用的旧委婉语。

intro.en: Professional is profession plus -al. English adds -ly, -ism, -ize, and the negative un-, while the Latin fateri also gives confess and confession.
intro.cn: professional 是 profession 加 -al。英语加 -ly、-ism、-ize 与否定 un-，拉丁语 fateri 还生成 confess 与 confession。

latinIntro.en: Latin professio 'public declaration' and profiteri 'declare openly' combine pro- 'forth' with fateri 'admit'. The family is about public avowal, not merely employment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”与 profiteri“公开宣称”把 pro-“向外”与 fateri“承认”结合。这个词族关乎公开表态，而不只是就业。

the process of becoming a profession

definition_zh: 教授；（大学的）教师；公开宣称者
definition_en: a senior teacher at a university, holding a chair or a high academic post, or a title used for such a person
core_image: 一位头发花白的学者站在讲台后，把一门学问当众讲给满堂学生
scene: 阶梯教室里坐满学生，讲台后的老人先把当天的争论讲清楚，再让学生自己反驳。The professor spent the first ten minutes answering questions about the reading.
sceneCN: 这里表示「大学教授」（第 1 个义项：在大学里拥有教席或高级学术职位的教师）；句意为教授用开头十分钟回答关于阅读材料的问题。

pos.zh: 教授；大学教师；公开宣称者

derivatives.zh: 由 professor 加 -ial 构成，义为「教授的；有教授派头的」
由 professor 加 -ship 构成，义为「教授职位」
由 professor 加 -iate 构成，义为「教授群体；教授职位」

senses.title: A senior university teacher with a chair or high post
senses.definition: a university teacher of the highest rank, usually holding a chair in a subject
senses.definitionCN: 大学中等级最高的教师，通常在某学科拥有教席
senses.example: She was made a professor at thirty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 她三十五岁时被聘为教授。
senses.why: The Latin word was simply a person who declares publicly; the medieval university gave that declarer a fixed place and rank, and the title followed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词本只是「公开发言的人」；中世纪的大学给这种公开讲授者固定的位置与等级，教授这一头衔便由此而来。

senses.title: A title placed before a name
senses.definition: a title used before the name of someone who holds such a post
senses.definitionCN: 用在拥有该职位者姓名之前的称呼
senses.example: Professor Lane will see you now.
senses.exampleCN: 莱恩教授现在可以见你了。
senses.why: Once the post became recognised, the name of the post turned into a form of address, shortened in speech but kept whole in writing.
senses.whyCN: 职位一旦被公认，职位的名称就变成了对人的称呼；口语里常简化，书面里仍写全。

senses.title: Any teacher at an American college
senses.definition: in American usage, a teacher at a college or university of any rank
senses.definitionCN: 在美式用法中，指学院或大学里任何级别的教师
senses.example: My professor assigned two chapters for Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 我的老师布置了周五要读的两章。
senses.why: American campuses applied the grand title to ordinary instructors, so the word widened from the chair-holder to almost anyone who teaches there.
senses.whyCN: 美国校园把这一显赫头衔套在普通讲师身上，于是词义从「拥有教席者」扩大到几乎所有在那里教书的人。

senses.title: A person who declares a belief publicly
senses.titleCN: 公开宣称者；信仰表白者
senses.definition: a person who makes an open declaration, especially of religious faith
senses.definitionCN: 公开做出声明的人，尤指公开表白宗教信仰者
senses.example: The early professors of the faith met in secret.
senses.exampleCN: 早期公开表白信仰的人秘密聚会。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense, still visible in the word's shape: the professor is the one who professes.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语的字面义，今天仍能从词的构造看出来：professor 就是「做公开声明的那个人」。

intro.en: Professor and profession share one Latin verb: profession names the declared work, while professor names the person who declares it.
intro.cn: professor 与 profession 共用一个拉丁动词：profession 指被声明的工作，professor 则指做声明的人。

items.en: Fateri meant to confess or acknowledge, to say openly something about oneself.
items.cn: fateri 意为承认、供认，即公开说出关于自己的事。

items.en: With pro-, the verb became profiteri, to declare publicly, whether a belief or a calling.
items.cn: 加上前缀 pro-，动词成为 profiteri，意为公开声明，对象可以是信仰，也可以是志业。

items.en: Professor was the agent noun: the person who professes, who declares openly, often a teacher of a doctrine.
items.cn: professor 是施动名词：做公开声明的人，常指某学说的讲授者。

items.en: In the medieval university a professor was one who publicly taught and disputed, and the word became tied to a teaching post.
items.cn: 在中世纪大学里，professor 指公开讲授并参与论辩的人，这个词遂与教职绑定。

items.en: English kept the academic sense as the main one, widened it in America to any college teacher, and let the religious sense fade.
items.cn: 英语以学术义为主，又在美国用法中扩大到任何大学教师，宗教义则逐渐淡去。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin family, including the noun for the declared work; the second gathers words for people who teach.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族，包括指「被声明的工作」的那个名词；第二组收表示教书育人之人的词。

entries.definition: To declare openly that one holds a belief or does a kind of work.
entries.definitionCN: 公开声明自己持某种信念或从事某种工作。

entries.definition: The declared work or calling, rather than the person who declares it.
entries.definitionCN: 被公开认领的职业或志业，指事不指人。

entries.definition: Relating to a profession, or a person who works in one.
entries.definitionCN: 与职业有关的；从事某一职业的人。

entries.definition: A person who confesses, or a priest who hears confession.
entries.definitionCN: 忏悔者；听人告解的司铎。

entries.definition: A teacher at a university below professorial rank.
entries.definitionCN: 大学中低于教授级别的教师；讲师。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to help others learn.
entries.definitionCN: 以帮助他人学习为业的人。

entries.definition: A person who teaches or researches at a university.
entries.definitionCN: 在大学任教或做研究的人。

entries.definition: A person who studies a subject deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 深入研究某一学科的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is the agent noun of a Latin verb of public declaring, and its history runs from the street speaker to the university chair.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「公开声明」动词的施动名词，它的历史从街头的发言者一路走到大学的教席。

normal.en: Professor ends in -or, the Latin ending for the doer, so it means the one who professes.
normal.cn: professor 以 -or 结尾，这是拉丁语表示「做事者」的词尾，所以它指「做声明的人」。

normal.en: The verb behind it is profiteri, to declare openly; a professor is literally a public declarer.
normal.cn: 背后的动词是 profiteri，意为公开声明；professor 字面上就是「公开声明者」。

normal.en: Profession is the declared work, professor the declarer, so the two words split one idea into thing and person.
normal.cn: profession 是被声明的工作，professor 是声明者，两个词把同一个意思拆成了「事」与「人」。

normal.en: The academic sense grew in medieval universities, where teaching was a public act of declaring a doctrine.
normal.cn: 学术义在中世纪大学里长成，因为当时的讲课就是公开声明某种学说的行为。

normal.en: In America the title spread to all college teachers, which is why students there call any instructor professor.
normal.cn: 在美国，这一头衔扩散到所有大学教师，所以那里的学生管任何讲师都叫 professor。

abstract.en: A professor is proof that teaching was once a form of public speech, not a private exchange of notes.
abstract.cn: professor 证明教学曾经是一种公开言说，而不是私下交换笔记。

abstract.en: The same root ties the classroom to the pulpit: to profess was first to declare a faith aloud.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根把课堂与讲坛系在一起：profess 最初就是大声宣告信仰。

abstract.en: A title that once meant one who speaks in public now marks one who is allowed to be heard.
abstract.cn: 这个头衔原指在公众面前说话的人，如今标记的是「有资格被听见」的人。

examples.en: The professor answered questions for ten minutes before the lecture.
examples.cn: 教授在开讲前回答了十分钟问题。

examples.en: Professor Hall has taught chemistry here for twenty years.
examples.cn: 霍尔教授在这里教了二十年化学。

examples.en: He was appointed professor of history last autumn.
examples.cn: 他去年秋天被聘为历史学教授。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「铺若费舌」——教授在讲台上把知识铺开，费尽口舌；记住 professor 是教授。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（公开、向前）+ fateri（承认）→ profiteri（公开声明）→ professor（公开宣称者，后指公开讲授者），经中世纪大学用语进入英语；与 profession 同源，一为「声明/职业」，一为「声明者」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who declares publicly; the academic post, the title before a name, the American widening and the old religious declarer all branch from that figure.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开做声明的人」；学术职位、姓名前的称谓、美式用法的扩大，以及旧时的宗教宣称者，都从这个人影分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scholar behind a lectern, declaring a subject aloud to a room of listeners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位学者站在讲台后，当众向满屋听众讲明一门学问。

branches.en: a chair-holder whose name is spoken with a title
branches.cn: 拥有教席、名字前带称谓的人

branches.en: a lecture hall filling before the first word
branches.cn: 开讲之前逐渐坐满的讲堂

branches.en: a student asking any instructor for help
branches.cn: 学生向任何一位讲师求助

branches.en: a small gathering declaring a faith in secret
branches.cn: 一小群人在暗中表白信仰

branches.en: a name card reading professor at the top
branches.cn: 名片最上方印着教授字样

intro.en: A Latin verb of public declaring, its prefix and its agent ending, plus the English endings that turn the person into a post and a quality, hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示公开声明的拉丁动词、它的前缀与施动词尾，再加上把「人」变成职位与性质的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: one who professes, a public teacher
items.meaningCN: 公开宣称者；公开讲授者

definition_zh: 熟练的；精通的；（语言）达到工作水平的
definition_en: able to do something well and effectively, at a level good enough for real work
core_image: 一位乐手不看谱也能把整段协奏曲拉完，手指在弦上几乎没有停顿
scene: 排练时乐手不看谱便把整段协奏曲拉完，指挥只偶尔点头。By her third year she was proficient on the cello.
sceneCN: 乐手三年后不看谱也能完整拉完协奏曲；句中的 proficient 指「熟练到足以实际运用」（第 1 个义项：在真实任务中能独立做好）。图中可辨识物件：大提琴、弓、谱架、节拍器。

senses.title: Skilled enough for real work
senses.definition: able to carry out a task well without close supervision
senses.definitionCN: 能在没有密切监督的情况下把任务做好
senses.example: By her third year she was proficient on the cello.
senses.exampleCN: 到第三年，她已经能熟练地演奏大提琴。
senses.why: proficere means 'to make progress', so the adjective marks someone who has got far enough to work, not someone who has merely begun.
senses.whyCN: proficere 意为「取得进展」，因此这个形容词标记的是已经走到能做事的人，而不是刚刚起步的人。

senses.title: A working level in a language
senses.definition: able to use a language for ordinary professional or academic purposes
senses.definitionCN: 能把一种语言用于日常的职业或学术目的
senses.example: He is proficient in English and can chair a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他英语熟练，能够主持会议。
senses.why: language testing fixed the adjective at a working band: enough to function, not necessarily native-like.
senses.whyCN: 语言测试把这个形容词固定在「工作水平」这一档：足以运转，不必像母语者。

senses.title: Technically skilled
senses.definition: practised in the use of a tool, instrument or technique
senses.definitionCN: 在使用工具、仪器或技法方面经过练习
senses.example: The lab hires only proficient technicians.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室只聘用熟练的技术员。
senses.why: the adjective attaches easily to tools because skill with a tool can be seen at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词很容易与工具连用，因为用工具的技艺一看便知。

senses.title: An advanced learner, as a noun
senses.titleCN: 名词用法：学有所成者（罕用）
senses.definition: a person who has reached an advanced level, especially in a language
senses.definitionCN: 达到较高水平的人，尤指在语言方面
senses.example: The class moved the proficients into a separate reading group.
senses.exampleCN: 班上把学有所成者分进另一个阅读组。
senses.why: the rare noun turns the adjective into a person, a usage kept alive mainly in language teaching.
senses.whyCN: 罕用的名词用法把形容词变成人，这种用法主要活在语言教学里。

senses.title: Effective in practice
senses.definition: doing what is needed competently rather than merely knowing about it
senses.definitionCN: 把需要的事做得像样，而不只是知道怎么做
senses.example: A proficient manager settles the dispute before it spreads.
senses.exampleCN: 一位称职的管理者会在争执扩散前把它解决。
senses.why: the word always points at performance: proficiency is shown in what gets done, not in what is claimed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终指向实际表现：熟练显现在做成的事上，而非宣称上。

senses.title: Showing mastery in performance
senses.definition: performing with control and assurance that practice has produced
senses.definitionCN: 以练习带来的控制力与把握完成表演
senses.example: Her proficient handling of the difficult passage drew applause.
senses.exampleCN: 她处理那段难句时显出功力，赢得掌声。
senses.why: in the arts the adjective praises control: the notes are not merely correct but securely held.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术中，这个形容词称赞的是控制力：音符不仅正确，而且握得稳。

senses.title: Trained and qualified
senses.definition: having completed the training that a role requires
senses.definitionCN: 已完成某个岗位所要求的训练
senses.example: Only proficient operators may run the press.
senses.exampleCN: 只有熟练的操作员才能开这台压机。
senses.why: qualification adds a gate: training ends when a person is judged proficient enough to be trusted alone.
senses.whyCN: 「合格」加上一道闸门：训练在一人被判定熟练到可以独自负责时结束。

senses.title: Capable but not an expert
senses.definition: good enough for the task at hand while falling short of mastery
senses.definitionCN: 足以应付眼前任务，但尚未达到精通
senses.example: He is proficient, though not yet expert, at repairing watches.
senses.exampleCN: 他修表已算熟练，但还称不上专家。
senses.why: the comparative scale leaves room above proficient; the word marks a threshold passed, not a summit reached.
senses.whyCN: 比较级量表在 proficient 之上还留有空间；这个词标记的是已过的门槛，而非登上的顶峰。

intro.en: Proficient is the present participle of Latin proficere 'to make progress, accomplish', built on pro- 'forward' and facere 'to do, make'. It entered English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: proficient 是拉丁 proficere「取得进展、完成」的现在分词，由 pro-「向前」与 facere「做、造」构成，于十六世纪进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Facere 'to do, make' is the root behind fact, effect, defect and every English verb in -fy.
items.cn: facere「做、造」是 fact、effect、defect 以及一切由它构成的英语动词背后的词根。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus facere gave proficere 'to make progress, to accomplish, to be of use'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 facere 给出 proficere「取得进展、完成、有用」。

items.en: The present participle proficiens described someone in the middle of making progress, hence 'getting somewhere, effective'.
items.cn: 现在分词 proficiens 描述正处在进展中的人，因此意为「走得到地方的、有效的」。

items.en: English adopted proficient in the sixteenth century, at first for things that were useful, then for people well advanced in a skill.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪采用 proficient，先指事物有用，后指人在技能上进展良好。

items.en: Twentieth-century language testing gave the adjective a fixed working band, so a certificate can state that someone is proficient rather than fluent.
items.cn: 二十世纪的语言测试给这个形容词一个固定的工作档位，于是证书可以写明某人为熟练而非流利。

items.en: The pre-Latin origin of facere is generally connected to a root meaning 'to put, set', but the exact chain is a reconstruction, and the sixteenth-century sense development is only partly documented.
items.cn: facere 在拉丁语之前的来源一般被认为与表示「放置」的词根相关，但确切链条属重构，十六世纪的语义发展也只有部分记录。

note.en: Group one holds the noun and the prefix siblings that look alike; group two holds adjectives of ability that claim different degrees.
note.cn: 第一组是名词形式以及形近的前缀同族词；第二组是表示能力的形容词，各自宣称的程度不同。

entries.definition: The measured level; proficient describes the person who holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被测出的水平；proficient 描述拥有这个水平的人。

entries.definition: Describes how a task is done, not what a person is.
entries.definitionCN: 描述任务如何被完成，而非人怎样。

entries.definition: From ex- plus facere: getting results with little waste, which says nothing about skill level.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex- 加 facere：以很少耗费取得结果，与技能水平无关。

entries.definition: From sub- plus facere: enough in amount, a quantity word rather than a skill word.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sub- 加 facere：数量上足够，是数量词而非技能词。

entries.definition: The plain adjective for training and practice; proficient adds the sense of being good enough for real work.
entries.definitionCN: 指受过训练与练习的普通形容词；proficient 多出「足以实际工作」之意。

entries.definition: Meets the required standard, sometimes no more than that; proficient usually implies a firmer command.
entries.definitionCN: 达到要求的标准，有时仅止于此；proficient 通常意味着更稳的掌控。

entries.definition: Smooth and rapid in speech, with less attention to accuracy or range than proficient.
entries.definitionCN: 说话顺滑快速，对准确度与覆盖面不如 proficient 看重。

entries.definition: A far higher claim than proficient: recognized mastery in a narrow field.
entries.definitionCN: 比 proficient 高得多的说法：在狭窄领域被认可的精通。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real Latin participle, the real family and the real threshold the word marks.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的拉丁分词、真实词族，以及这个词所标记的真实门槛。

normal.en: proficiens is a participle: someone in the middle of getting somewhere.
normal.cn: proficiens 是分词：一个正走到某处的人。

normal.en: pro- 'forward' plus facere 'do': moving forward in what one does.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 facere「做」：在做的事上向前走。

normal.en: The family runs proficient, proficiency, proficiently.
normal.cn: 词族包括 proficient、proficiency、proficiently。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the test: proficient in, highly proficient, proficient user.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出测试语境：在……熟练、高度熟练、熟练使用者。

normal.en: The word marks a threshold, so it pairs with enough and not yet: proficient enough, not yet expert.
normal.cn: 这个词标记门槛，因此常与「够」和「尚未」连用：够熟练、尚未精通。

abstract.en: Picture a musician who no longer needs the score but still keeps it open.
abstract.cn: 想象一位乐手已不再需要看谱，却仍把谱子摊开。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox whose every handle is worn smooth in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只工具箱，每个把手的同一处都被磨得光滑。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked with a line at shoulder height, already passed.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在齐肩高处画了一道线，而人已走过它。

examples.en: She became proficient in Spanish after two summers abroad.
examples.cn: 在国外度过两个夏天后，她的西班牙语变得熟练。

examples.en: A proficient reader adjusts speed to the difficulty of the text.
examples.cn: 熟练的读者会按文本难度调整速度。

examples.en: The workshop produces proficient welders in six months.
examples.cn: 这个工作坊六个月就能培养出熟练的焊工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ fic（做）」——越做越往前 → 熟练的、精通的

root: 拉丁 pro-「向前」+ facere「做」→ proficere「取得进展」→ 现在分词 proficiens → 英语 proficient；facere 的更早来源一般与「放置」词根相关，确切链条属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one threshold: a learner has moved far enough forward to do real work, and the threshold is then applied to a language, a tool, a classroom role, a dispute, a performance, a licence and a repair bench.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用一个门槛：学习者向前走到足以做真实工作的位置，这个门槛随后用于语言、工具、课堂角色、争执、表演、执照与修理台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on a doorframe at shoulder height, already crossed, with more height still available above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：门框上齐肩高处的一道线，人已跨过，而线上方仍有余地。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD: the same line separates training from trusted independent work.
branches.cn: 门槛：同一条线把训练与可被信任的独立工作分开。

branches.en: THE LANGUAGE BAND: testing pins the threshold to a working level of a language.
branches.cn: 语言档位：测试把门槛固定在语言的工作水平上。

branches.en: HAND AND STAGE: a tool and a performance both show the threshold in execution.
branches.cn: 手与舞台：工具与表演都把门槛显现在执行之中。

branches.en: ROLE AND PRACTICE: the rare noun names the person, and effective practice proves the claim.
branches.cn: 角色与实践：罕用名词指人，有效的实践则证明这份宣称。

branches.en: ROOM ABOVE: mastery lies beyond the line, so proficient never means finished.
branches.cn: 线上余地：精通在门槛之外，因此 proficient 从不意味「到头」。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin prefix and root plus a participle ending, and the same pieces build the whole proficiency family.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由拉丁前缀、词根加一个分词词尾构成，同一批部件造出整个 proficiency 词族。

latinIntro.en: Pro- and facere build proficere; its present participle proficiens is the direct source of the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: pro- 与 facere 构成 proficere；其现在分词 proficiens 是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 分词词尾表示进行与主动。

items.example: The adjective entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词于十六世纪进入英语。
